tim: FYI — following up on the streaming chat postmortem (linked below). We identified a recurring pattern: intermittent partial responses + client reconnects in eu-west during high burst windows. I opened this thread to capture owners/timelines and a lightweight weekly pulse. https://redwood.example/postmortem/streaming-2026-03

maria: thanks. confirming i'll own the reconnect-logic item (investigate sticky connection state + backpressure). Targeting a prototype fix by EOW next week.

alex: i'll take the partial-response mitigation (kv cache invalidation edge cases + small-batch fallback). ETA 2 weeks, unless we need a hotfix.

ryan: product asks for a customer-facing summary and a comms plan if we roll a change to client SDKs that could impact session semantics. i'll draft a short note for the SRE & support playbook.

tim: note on priority — SLA-sensitive customers get immediate routing to dedicated pools; hosted users may see transient partials. We should have a temporary mitigant: auto-retry on short HTTP streams with increasing backoff and idempotency key. Can eng-sre prototype a circuit-breaker rule?

sre-lead: i can put a canary rule in place for eu-west tomorrow morning: limit inflight streaming sessions per node and apply 2s jittered reconnect backoff. Will monitor 5m error-rate and token drop counts.

oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled follow-up check-in in 7 days (channel: #incidents). Please add task IDs to this thread with the format HF-<number>.

maria: quick note — found a repro: client sends a second partial ACK which causes the server session to treat stream as closed, leads to KV cache eviction. snippet from logs:
```
2026-03-02T14:12:03Z STREAM_CONN  node=gs-12 event=partial_ack seq=342 session=abcd1234
2026-03-02T14:12:04Z STREAM_CONN  node=gs-12 event=partial_ack seq=343 session=abcd1234
2026-03-02T14:12:04Z KVCACHE     node=gs-12 action=evict session=abcd1234 reason=duplicate_ack
```
This suggests we need stricter ACK dedup semantics and a short grace window before eviction.

alex: good catch. i'll add a unit behavior test around duplicate ACKs and a 150ms grace window before evicting KV. Will post PR link here when ready (HF-4217).

tim: thanks. owners & rough dates: maria (reconnect sticky state) — 2026-03-09; alex (kv cache grace + tests) — 2026-03-16 (HF-4217); sre-lead (canary rule) — 2026-03-03; ryan (customer comms) — 2026-03-05. If anyone needs to shift dates, reply with updated ETA.

ryan: adding note — if fixes alter session semantics we should include a config toggle in the SDK so existing integrations can opt-in initially. i'll coordinate with devex.

maria: ack on opt-in toggle. i'll design the server-side toggle and a migration plan for 30-day opt-in window. HF-4218.

oncall-bot: HF task tracker updated: HF-4217, HF-4218, HF-4219 (canary rule), HF-4220 (comm-ops).

tim: can we also capture recurrence pattern analysis? alex can you run a 90-day query for partial response rate by region, model-size, and sequence-length bucket and paste the output? small ask but will help prioritization.

alex: will run the query and post a short table here by EOD. preliminary glance shows spikes correlate with requests >2048 tokens and with 2 specific older model variants.

sre-lead: once canary goes live i'll chart rolling 1h drop-rate and trigger an automated rollback if drop-rate > 0.8% over baseline for 3 consecutive windows.

tim: great. final ask: recurring 30-min weekly sync in this thread (or brief updates) until all HF tasks are closed. i'll drop a calendar invite for a 15-min slot tomorrow. :thumbsup:

maria: :thumbsup: adding daily short status notes here until my PR merges.

alex: posting query results in a follow-up comment (HF-4217) — will keep this thread updated.

ryan: i'll prepare the customer-facing note draft and share for review before publish.

sre-lead: canary scheduled for 2026-03-03 06:00 UTC. monitoring runbook updated and linked in the incident doc.

oncall-bot: Follow-up check-in (7 days) scheduled. Tasks open: HF-4217, HF-4218, HF-4219, HF-4220.

tim: thanks everyone — i'll mark this thread as the primary remediation tracker. If you post task updates, start the message with the HF number so the bot can index it.
